subject: MSA orderflow: provisional injunctive protocol + jurisdiction fallback matrix
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CloudScale MSA redlines — urgent guidance on injunctive scope and forum fallback

Team — forwarding CloudScale's redline (attached). They have pushed two asks that will matter for how we operate the Dedicated offering:

1) Broad injunctive relief carveout: they want a clause that would allow them to seek immediate injunctive relief in their local courts for alleged data misuse, even if the MSA routes most disputes to arbitration.
2) Choice-of-jurisdiction toggle: they propose language that would let them select their home-country courts for "emergency measures" but require arbitration for all other disputes; language is vague about what qualifies as an emergency.

Sales context: this is a strategic mid-market account (expected first-year ARR $420k). We have scope sensitivity on being able to rely on arbitration/fixed forum for the bulk of disputes to avoid ad-hoc injunctive litigation that could force data center-level actions.

Ask: Mina/Law — can you propose a short, defensible fallback matrix and a limited injunctive carveout we can offer as counter? Ideally: (a) allow emergency provisional remedies in local courts but limit to preservation measures and prohibit ex parte asset seizures or service termination; (b) require a narrow, objective trigger (credible risk to PII/confidentiality with supporting affidavit).

I've attached their redline and a quick xlsx that maps our preferred forum outcomes to their asks.

Thanks — Nikhil

Attachment: CloudScale_MSA_redline_20270917.docx (redline — ~15 pages)
Attachment: provisional-remedies-matrix.xlsx (draft compromise matrix)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CloudScale MSA redlines — urgent guidance on injunctive scope and forum fallback

Nikhil — reviewed. High-level thoughts:

- We should accept a narrow emergency relief carveout but define the remedy set tightly. Suggested language (short form) to propose to the counterparty: "Notwithstanding Section X (Arbitration), either party may seek provisional injunctive or other emergency relief in a court of competent jurisdiction solely to preserve the status quo or to prevent imminent and irreparable harm to the confidentiality or integrity of Customer Data. Such relief shall be limited to preservation measures and shall not include orders for specific performance that would require ongoing operational changes or asset seizure. Any party seeking emergency relief will: (i) identify the specific data or system at risk; (ii) submit a sworn statement describing the imminent harm; and (iii) use commercially reasonable efforts to notify the other party and the arbitrator."
- For forum fallback: propose a three-line matrix we can offer — (1) Emergency preservation measures = local courts (limited scope, as above), (2) Data privacy statutory claims where injunctive relief is sought = courts in customer's seat but only on statutory questions; arbitration remains for contract claims, (3) All other disputes = binding arbitration in Delaware under AAA rules.

- Risk tradeoff: allowing local courts for preservation reduces friction for customers in regulated markets. But we must ensure the carveout cannot be used to obtain broad injunctive remedies that force service changes. The inclusion of required affidavit and notice is helpful.

I drafted tracker comments in the attached redline (see CloudScale_MSA_redline_20270917.docx). I also populated provisional-remedies-matrix.xlsx with the three-line fallback.

If you want, I can draft a short explanatory paragraph (2–3 lines) for Emma to soften the legal framing when we send the counterproposal through Sales.

-Mina

Attachment: CloudScale_MSA_redline_20270917.docx (with inline comments)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Emma Rios <emma.rios@cloudscale.com>
Cc: CloudScale Legal <legal@cloudscale.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CloudScale MSA — proposed compromise on provisional remedies and dispute forum

Emma — thanks for the quick redline. We appreciate CloudScale flagging the need to move fast when data is at risk. We pulled together a short, pragmatic compromise that preserves your ability to get urgent preservation relief while protecting both parties from open-ended forum-shopping.

Proposed (high level):
- Emergency preservation measures: either party may seek provisional injunctive relief in local courts limited to preserving data/systems and preventing imminent, irreparable harm. No relief that compels long-term operational changes or asset seizure.
- Objective trigger: must include a sworn statement describing the imminent harm and identify the affected data/system.
- Main disputes: arbitration (Delaware, AAA) for contract claims; statutory privacy claims tied to injunctive relief may proceed in Customer's seat only for the limited statutory issue.

I've attached the marked redline and a short matrix that lays this out. If you're okay in principle, can we get CloudScale Legal's comment by EOD Tuesday so we can finalize for DocuSign? We're hoping to keep the orderform timeline intact.

Best — Nikhil

Attachments referenced: CloudScale_MSA_redline_20270917.docx, provisional-remedies-matrix.xlsx

From: Emma Rios <emma.rios@cloudscale.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudScale Legal <legal@cloudscale.com>
Date: 2027-09-19T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CloudScale MSA — proposed compromise on provisional remedies and dispute forum

Nikhil — appreciate the practical framing. CloudScale Legal reviewed and provided two small edits:

1) Add ability for expedited (ex parte) temporary relief in cases where notice would defeat the purpose — limited to preservation of evidence and preservation of access controls (they moved to include a carveout for ex parte narrowly defined).
2) Narrow the Delaware arbitration to allow our EU subsidiary to elect Dublin courts for statutory data protection measures if the underlying data subject requests local remedies.

We suggest the following path: (a) accept Redwood's preservation-only carveout but (b) add a narrowly worded ex parte sentence and (c) include a limited subsidiary seat exception for statutory DPAs. Attached is the updated redline and a DocuSign envelope we can push once you sign off.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/CLD-4287-signature

Regards,
Emma

Attachment: CloudScale_MSA_redline_20270919.docx (their edits)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CloudScale MSA — proposed compromise on provisional remedies and dispute forum

Nikhil — OK to proceed with minor tweaks. My recommended final positions:

- Keep preservation-only carveout language but explicitly prohibit service-stopping orders and asset transfer.
- For ex parte narrow carveout: accept only when (i) the party demonstrates that immediate notice would frustrate preservation and (ii) relief is limited to evidence preservation and temporary access controls. Add a 7-day follow-up hearing provision.
- For subsidiary seat exception: agree to permit an EU subsidiary to seek statutory DPA remedies in Dublin/local DPAs, but add a clause that such statutory claims are limited to data-protection statute remedies and do not alter arbitration rights for contractual disputes between the parties.

Propose we send the redline back with a 1–2 paragraph plain-language summary (I will draft) highlighting the mutual desire to avoid forum-shopping while protecting data. If Sales wants me on the call with Emma for the final close, I can join.

-Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
